name: ux_antipatterns
caption: The endless-panes antipattern catalog (by product spread).
sql: SELECT pattern, len(exemplar_product_ids) n_products, hci_cost, our_stance FROM market.ux_patterns WHERE is_antipattern ORDER BY n_products DESC LIMIT 25

rows.pattern: Canvas-based rendering (SVG or WebGL) provides no semantic HTML structure for screen readers; node relationships and graph topology inaccessible to assistive technology
All 5 platforms (Zapier, Make, n8n, Node-RED, Latenode) require users to specify field mappings during workflow build, not upfront. Changing upstream app = cascading rework downstream.
Information revealed only on mouse hover (edge labels, node descriptions, connection metadata)
Low-Code Platforms Reduce Visible Code, but Increase Hidden UI Complexity (Config UI becomes new 'code')
Platforms Target 'Citizen Developers' (Non-Technical Users) But Require 2-4 Week Learning Curve (Reduces Adoption)
100+ UI Components in Visual Builder, Requiring Cognitive Categorization
Node-Link Graphs Cluttered at Scale (>30 nodes)
Modal-Heavy Workflows: Multi-Step Forms in Dialogs
Graph visualization requires simultaneous visibility of 4-5 UI panels (canvas, layout controls, property inspector, style editor, element details) to access full functionality
Fine-Grained Role-Based Access Control Exposed as Feature Matrix (8+ role types, per-resource assignment)
Left Inspector + Center Canvas + Right Properties Pane (3-Pane Layout)
Graph query language (Cypher, GQL, Gremlin) required to perform advanced operations, blocking non-technical users
Performance Blindness (No Query Cost Visibility Before Execution)

Platforms with code fallback (Latenode, Node-RED, n8n JavaScript expressions) allow users to 'code their way out' of visual limitations, but this creates context-switching overhead (visual editor ↔ code editor) and discourages learning the visual paradigm.
Nested Modal Dialogs: Trigger-Action-Condition-Value Matrices
AI Features (Text-to-Diagram, Clustering, Summarization) as Separate Tools, Not Integrated into Main Canvas
Multiple persistent panes (3-6 simultaneous panels/sidebars) forcing user eye-scanning and context-switching between controls and canvas
Offline vs. Online Mode Cognitive Split
End-users forced to select and tune graph layout algorithms (force-directed, hierarchical, circular, etc.) with technical parameters (iterations, spring length, gravity)
Critical operations (select all, layout, undo/redo, search) hidden behind undocumented keyboard shortcuts with no visual hint or menu entry
Query Language Barrier (Cypher/nGQL/SQL Required)
Unbounded Query Results (No Default Limit, Large Clutter)
Feature Comparison Matrix as Pricing/Plan Selector
Hourly Usage-Based or Tiered Per-User Pricing Creates Uncertainty in TCO Calculation
Dashboard design requires manual layout, data variant handling, and extensive user testing with real data
